metadata.title: Res Nova: Geometrically Ordered Dynamics and Information Tension — Dual-Channel Action, Covariant Completion, and Formal Verification
metadata.description: The dual-channel action F_dual(x) = ½x² - x + ln(1+x) has constitutive ratio F'(x)/x equal to the MOND interpolation function μ(x) = x/(1+x). Given four structural constraints — constitutive-relation form, Padé[1/1] minimality, the MOND boundary conditions, and dual-channel splitting — F_dual is uniquely determined; the necessity of the Padé constraint is not derived, so the uniqueness is conditional. Embedded in the Skordis-Złośnik (2021) RMOND framework, the linear screening ratio F''/F' ≈ 0.004 reduces a 76× structure overproduction to 0.4% in linear growth, and Vainshtein screening places the solar-system quadrupole at Q₂ ≈ 4.9×10⁻²⁹ s⁻², a factor 70 below the Cassini bound at natural O(1) couplings. Ghost-free with c_T = c. 21 Lean 4 modules verified, no sorry, axioms restricted to {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, including exact Cartan Triality fermion generation count (N_gen = 3) and Ramanujan-Chladni nodal harmonic mass hierarchy. SPARC 175-galaxy benchmark; a₀ = (1.116 ± 0.016)×10⁻¹⁰ m/s². A pre-registered a₀(z) test favours constant a₀ over the horizon-tied a₀(z) = ξcH(z) at 5.9σ.
